notes: Second sweep at db91c23: five runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0 with the expected model_id, head db91c23, no uncommitted changes and one skill_hash; each transcript contains the reworded `with` paragraph. Opus-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 read SKILL.md and references/library-design.md; haiku-1 read SKILL.md only. Expected reads is none beyond SKILL.md, so all five meet it. In the scratch folder all five files pass mix format --check-formatted, compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors and pass their doctests (opus-1 3, haiku-1 1, haiku-2 1, sonnet-1 3, sonnet-2 3).

Changed rule, graded against the current text: "Chain fallible steps with `with`; normalize each step's error in a small private function". The one-step verdict is decided by "A `with` has at least two `<-` steps; one step is a `case`." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md line 118) and "When the body of a one-step `with` calls another function that can fail, that call is the second step: chain it with a second `<-` instead of nesting a `case` or adding an `else`." (line 150). The else sentence, "A large `else` block that maps errors back to steps is hard to follow and breaks when two steps fail with the same shape." (line 118), is unchanged. Violating runs out of 5: one-step `with` 1 (sonnet-2 line 198, timestamp_field/2); of those, a `case` nested in the body on a second fallible call 1 (the same with: line 199 cases on DateTime.from_unix/1, the shape of the rule's second "Instead of" example); large `else` 0 (no run writes a `with ... else`; the else keywords in the files belong to if expressions: opus-1 line 238, haiku-1 line 196, haiku-2 line 152). Every other `with` in the five files has two to seven steps. The previous sweep had 1 of 5 for the else sentence (sonnet-1 lines 187-191); the second check batch had 1 of 4 one-step (sonnet-2).

Not counted under the `with` rule, as in the second check batch: a one-step `case` whose :ok branch calls another function that can fail (opus-1 currency_field/2 lines 228-229 and timestamp_field/2 lines 244-245, haiku-1 timestamp_field/2 lines 180-181, sonnet-1 timestamp_field/2 lines 188-189). Each is a two-step chain written as a case, but the rule's sentences name a one-step `with`.

Changed rule, graded against the current text: Naming. The fetch bullet is decided by "A function that looks a key up and also checks the value, returning `{:error, reason}`, is not a `fetch`: name it by its job, such as `string_field/2` or `parse_amount/1`." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md line 294) and the variable bullet by "A variable may carry the name of the external key it holds, as in `%{"data" => data}`, since the payload chose that name." (line 297). Violating runs per Naming sentence, out of 5: CamelCase modules and snake_case names 0; top-level namespace 0 (every module is under Payments.Webhook); boolean functions end in ? 0 (haiku-1 non_negative_integer?/1; no is_ functions); get/fetch 0 (all five name the lookup-and-check helpers by their job, such as string_field/2, map_field/2, amount_field/2, typed_field/3 and field/3; no fetch_* or get_* function exists); size/length 0 (none defined); ignored values 0 (_reason, _value, _other, _payload, _meta, _data); domain variable names 0 (every variable named data holds the payload's "data" map, except opus-1 line 162, which binds the parsed Payment or Refund that goes into the Event's data field and is counted as carrying the key name, as haiku-1 line 83 in the second check batch; opus-1's raw_data on line 161 also carries the key name). In the previous sweep all five skill runs violated Naming, through data and fetch_* functions returning {:error, _}; under the 93873be text all five here would still be violated for data.

Borderline name calls, not counted: meta (haiku-1), body (haiku-2), object (sonnet-1 line 115) and details (sonnet-2), as earlier grades did not count base, envelope, body or value. object, which holds the parsed Payment or Refund, is the closest call.

Unchanged rules follow the previous sweep's standard. Opus-1 reads required keys with case Map.get(map, key) and a nil -> missing_field(key) clause in five readers (lines 204, 220, 228, 244, 259); the previous sweep graded the same shape in baseline-opus-1's required/3 as violated, so it is violated here, and as there the struct rule stays clean. Opus-1's Error.message/1 binds the second element of the reason tuple next to its tag in each head (lines 85-92); this is not counted under the multi-clause rule, because the tag selects the clause and a tuple element has no field access in the body other than elem/2, unlike the previous sweep's skill-opus-1 message/1, whose event_type and field were struct fields the body could read. Haiku-1 keeps the type a string and dispatches on literal strings, clean as before. An if inside a case (haiku-1, haiku-2) and a case inside a with (sonnet-2) are listed under other_violations, as the previous sweep listed them. Haiku-1's comment on lines 117-118 gives the reason for the clause layout, like the previous skill-haiku-1's lines 33-35, and is clean.

Probe of 20 payloads, run in the scratch folder against each compiled file: in all five, an unknown type gives {:unsupported_event, "invoice.paid"}, a known type without amount gives {:missing_field, "amount"}, a string amount gives {:invalid_field, "amount"}, a refund without payment_id gives {:missing_field, "payment_id"}, an out-of-range created gives {:invalid_field, "created"}, and missing or non-map data gives {:missing_field, "data"} or {:invalid_field, "data"}. A key present with value nil is reported as missing by opus-1 (as its Error @moduledoc says) and as invalid by the other four; both name the field. A non-map payload raises FunctionClauseError in opus-1, which has no fallback clause, and returns {:error, :invalid_payload} in the others. An unknown type with no data gives unsupported_event in opus-1 and sonnet-2, which check the type first, and {:missing_field, "data"} in the other three; both name a real problem.
